# Post Type Playbooks

Use these playbooks after checking [the full _posts corpus](../../../../docs/_posts) and selecting related source posts. These are recurring post patterns, not a permanent content taxonomy. If the author writes about something new, create a temporary playbook from the active draft, the audience of one, and the closest structural or tonal matches in the corpus.

Do not force a new topic into one of these sections. Borrow mechanics and rhythm from the closest useful model, then let the draft define the category.

Each section includes two canonical examples. They are stable structural models, not an exhaustive or automatically current index. Search the live corpus for the closest recent posts before relying on them.

## Technical Guides

Canonical examples:

1. [Reference Linked Services](../../../../docs/_posts/2024-05-18-reference-linked-services-synapse.md)
2. [GitHub Copilot Auto-Approve URLs](../../../../docs/_posts/2026-02-24-vscode-github-copilot-auto-approve-urls.md)

Pattern:

1. Open with the problem and context.
2. Show the syntax, screenshot, or code quickly.
3. Explain each moving part in plain language.
4. Link to docs or related resources.
5. End when the solution is complete.

Editorial risks: adding fluff, over explaining simple steps, removing practical screenshots, or making the tone too formal.

## AI, Software Engineering, And Career Commentary

Canonical examples:

1. [GitHub Copilot Agent Mode](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-02-15-github-copilot-agent-mode.md)
2. [Coding Is Dead, Software Engineering Isn't](../../../../docs/_posts/2026-02-02-coding-is-dead-software-engineering-isnt.md)

Pattern:

1. Establish why the topic matters right now.
2. Use personal industry context where relevant.
3. Mix skepticism with practical optimism.
4. Use GIFs and notices for reaction beats or navigation.
5. Close with a practical stance, not vague inspiration.

Editorial risks: generic AI hype, corporate phrasing, weak claims without links, or smoothing away the author's sharper opinions.

## STEM Workshops And Education

Canonical examples:

1. [Three Levels Of Programming](../../../../docs/_posts/2024-11-19-stem-workshop-three-levels-of-programming-petoi-bittle.md)
2. [AI Engineering With Petoi Bittle](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-07-23-ai-engineering-petoi-bittle.md)

Pattern:

1. Start with the personal reason this work matters.
2. Use a `Heads Up` notice when the intro is anecdotal and the workshop starts later.
3. Include required materials, required expertise, workshop overview, and resources.
4. Keep facilitator language practical and accessible.
5. Close with encouragement and useful links.

Editorial risks: sounding like curriculum marketing, losing the personal why, or skipping concrete facilitation details.

## Entertainment Review Or Analysis

Canonical examples:

1. [Attack On Titan](../../../../docs/_posts/2023-12-03-attack-on-titan-cemented-greatness.md)
2. [Things We Lost In The Fire](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-10-30-things-we-lost-in-the-fire.md)

Pattern:

1. Open with the cultural frame or direct thesis.
2. Add spoiler warnings when needed.
3. Make the personal stake visible.
4. Build from specific scenes or characters to the broader argument.
5. Use memes or embedded media as tone breaks.
6. Close by returning to the thesis.

Editorial risks: over formalizing fan language, cutting the jokes, or making a hot take sound timid.

## Faith Posts

Canonical examples:

1. [The Comforts Of Christ](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-02-27-comforts-of-christ.md)
2. [The Commands Of Christ](../../../../docs/_posts/2022-07-29-commands-of-christ.md)

Pattern:

1. Ground the post in personal need, Scripture, or reflection.
2. Let Scripture quotes create rhythm.
3. Link citations to BibleGateway or relevant sources.
4. Keep the tone humble, vulnerable, and clear.
5. Avoid turning reflection into performance.

Editorial risks: Shying away from the truth of the Gospel, adding theological claims without support, or flattening vulnerability.

## Dough Diaries, Food, Travel, And Third Places

Canonical examples:

1. [Dough Diaries Raleigh](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-01-31-dough-diaries-raleigh.md)
2. [Charlotte Third Places Tech Stack](../../../../docs/_posts/2024-09-24-charlotte-third-places-tech-stack.md)

Pattern:

1. Start with a personal discovery or conviction.
2. Be opinionated but self aware.
3. Use rankings only when they help.
4. Add location sections and Google Maps embeds when appropriate.
5. Close by inviting readers to form their own opinions.

Editorial risks: turning the post into a sterile review, cutting the digressions that make the piece human, or missing local context.

## Resource Compilations

Canonical examples:

1. [AI Learning Resources](../../../../docs/_posts/2024-05-05-ai-learning-resources.md)
2. [AI Resources For Educators](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-03-20-ai-resources-for-educators.md)

Pattern:

1. Explain who the list is for.
2. Group resources by reader stage or use case.
3. Use notice blocks for resource cards when that pattern fits.
4. Include free or paid context where useful.
5. Keep commentary practical and opinionated.

Editorial risks: becoming a link dump, over summarizing every item, or losing the author's guidance.

## Press, Personal Highlight, Or Link Posts

Canonical examples:

1. [CBJ 40 Under 40](../../../../docs/_posts/2025-05-16-cbj-40-under-40.md)
2. [Charlotte Observer Third Places Article](../../../../docs/_posts/2026-01-14-charlotte-third-places-observer-article.md)

Pattern:

1. Keep the metadata clean.
2. Use `link:` for external link posts when appropriate.
3. Add custom schema only when there is a clear high visibility reason.
4. Keep the body personal, grateful, and specific.

Editorial risks: generic press release language, over explaining the achievement, or missing the link post mechanics.
